title: Recurrent Meningitis Following Previous Repair of Congenital Oval Window Defect
case_prompt:
A 19-year-old man was referred for evaluation of recurrent bacterial meningitis. He first presented at age 7 with culture-proven meningitis and was found to have otitis media with effusion in the left ear. Persistent otorrhea after myringotomy prompted CT, which showed a left-sided type I incomplete partition deformity and a congenital oval window defect. He underwent canal-wall-down mastoidectomy and repair of the oval window defect, with two additional repairs after meningitis recurrences at ages 10 and 11. Each surgery localized CSF leaks, once at the oval window and once at the tegmen tympani, with subsequent pneumococcal vaccination.

On the current admission, he had fever, headache, and neck stiffness but no focal neurologic deficits; Kernig’s and Brudzinski’s signs were negative. Otoscopic examination of the left ear revealed an intact tympanic membrane and a large collection of fluid pulsating in the mastoid cavity and middle ear. There was no vestibular deficit, and nasoendoscopy showed no frank fluid draining from the left Eustachian tube. Audiometry revealed profound left hearing loss with normal right-sided hearing.

He was started empirically on ceftriaxone, vancomycin, and acyclovir. A lumbar puncture on hospital day 3 showed low glucose and high opening pressure consistent with bacterial meningitis, although cultures were negative. High-resolution CT of the temporal bones showed a widened left oval window and an absent stapes footplate with complete opacification of the middle ear and mastoid; the tegmen tympani appeared intact. T2-weighted MRI demonstrated fluid signals in the middle ear and mastoid that matched signals in the internal acoustic meatus and vestibule, along with an expanded internal acoustic meatus and distended Eustachian tube filled with similar fluid signal.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Consideration of otitis media with effusion — “the other differentials for the fluid signal in the middle ear include otitis media with effusion…”  
2. Consideration of granulation tissue from chronic otitis media — “…and granulation formation from chronic otitis media.”  
3. Suspected CSF leak through the oval window defect — “This raises the suspicion that there was likely CSF within the middle ear and mastoid, which is most probably leaking through the oval window defect and absent stapes footplate.”  
4. Exclusion of tegmen tympani leak — “…with an intact tegmen tympani.”
